About the Evening

When the sun softens, we show up.

August is National Black Business Month. When the sun begins its descent over the Eastside on August 23, something remarkable happens. The light softens. The air warms. People slow down — and they show up for one another.

Golden Hour Unboxed is a free, cross-cultural evening at Bellevue Botanical Garden where Black entrepreneurs, artists, families, and allies gather under the sunset to mingle, share, and rise together. It's a celebration of the many ways our community contributes to the Eastside — through art, food, storytelling, mentorship, and the everyday brilliance of building something from nothing.

This is more than an event. It's a platform — for emerging Black entrepreneurs to mingle with seasoned professionals. For families to experience cross-cultural exchange in real time. For artists, vendors, and community builders to be seen and supported.

Plan Your Visit

Find your way through the garden.

Golden Hour Unboxed is held at the Aaron Education Center inside Bellevue Botanical Garden — 12001 Main St, Bellevue, WA. Enter at the Garden Entrance by the parking lot; the Education Center is a short, accessible walk just past the entrance. Explore the full garden map and accessible routes below.

Come early and walk the garden. The Bellevue Botanical Garden is open to the public all afternoon — arrive whenever the light calls you, wander the pathways, and make an evening of it. The Aaron Education Center doors open at 5:30 PM for check-in; program begins at 6:00 PM.

“Keep the Receipt” · Melissa Margain

Storyteller for the Convening · 6:56

Every entrepreneur has receipts, and not just the ones printed on paper. Melissa’s piece is about the unseen investments behind every dream — the sacrifices, the setbacks, and the quiet acts of faith that never make the highlight reel.

An author, poet and speaker who collects stories the way some people collect passport stamps, she is drawn to the beautifully awkward, deeply human moments we usually keep to ourselves. A U.S. Army veteran with a career in public service, she is as comfortable in a boardroom as on an open mic stage.

All night, no schedule required

Twenty tables. Black-owned businesses and makers selling inside, community organizations out in the garden. Everything you buy goes straight to the person who made it.

Pack the Box, our school supply drive. The schools cover pencils now — what they don't cover is backpacks, water bottles, headphones, coats, hygiene items and classroom supplies. Gift cards are welcome and quietly our favorite.

The Black Hair Care Drive, out in the garden. Hair care products for young people across this county, now in its third year.

A donation station, staffed all evening. Cash or check. Gifts go through Eastside For All, our nonprofit partner, so your giving here is a charitable donation.

Community Initiative

Pack the Box.
Send a kid to school.

Bring back-to-school supplies and pack a box for a student in need. It's the easiest, warmest way to participate — bring a notebook or backpack, leave with new friends. Everything collected goes to the schools with the highest need, PreK through high school.

Whatever you give, whether supplies or a gift of any amount, is a tax-deductible charitable donation received through Eastside For All, a DBA of Alliance for a Just Society, a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization.

Storytellers for the Convening

The voices we'll gather around.

A small circle of founders, makers, and builders we have invited to carry their stories into the evening.

Each Storyteller for the Convening wears a corsage at the event. Look for the corsage and you have found someone with a story worth a moment of your time — about how they started, what they have built, and what they are still becoming. Stories happen on a walk through the garden, in conversation in the crowd, or briefly on stage as the sun softens.

Five storytellers. Three minutes each, on what it actually took to build the thing they built — including the parts that don't photograph well. Their names are announced from the stage on the night.

With Gratitude

Civic champions.

First voices in support — public servants who saw the vision early and lent their offices to lift Black Business Month on the Eastside.

Proclamation Received · August 4, 2026
"Bellevue welcomed me with wide open arms, and made room for me at table after table. I want every Black business owner building in this city to feel that — because every entrepreneur deserves that kind of welcome."

— Katoya R. Palmer, accepting the City of Bellevue's proclamation declaring August 2026 as Black Business Month, delivered by Deputy Mayor Dave Hamilton on behalf of Mayor Mo Malakoutian and the Bellevue City Council.

Watch the moment on TikTok →
Proclamation Signed · King County
"Black Business Month takes on particular meaning on the Eastside, where a new generation of Black founders, makers, and small business owners is reshaping the cultural and economic fabric of our communities."

— King County Executive Girmay Zahilay, proclaiming August 2026 as Black Business Month and recognizing Black Entrepreneurship on the Eastside. The proclamation will be read at Golden Hour Unboxed by Angela Phan, East County Relations Manager, King County Executive Office.

Why This Event

Bellevue is one of Washington's most diverse cities. Intentional spaces for Black entrepreneurs to be celebrated and seen by their neighbors are still rare on the Eastside.

Golden Hour Unboxed is a free, public evening built to close that gap — for Black entrepreneurs, their families, and the whole Eastside community that gathers around them.

We hold this gathering in August, during National Black Business Month, because the timing matters. We hold it at Bellevue Botanical Garden because the place matters. We hold it as part of the City of Bellevue's Cross-Cultural Center without Walls because the structure of belonging matters.

This isn't a passive cultural showcase. It's an active exchange — Black entrepreneurs, allies, and neighbors sharing names, ideas, and how to find each other after the sun sets.

FAQ

Questions, answered.

Still curious? Email katoya@toyboxconsulting.net and we'll get back to you.

Golden Hour Unboxed is free to the public per our agreement with Bellevue Botanical Garden. RSVP secures your spot but does not include a charge. Please RSVP so we can plan accordingly for refreshments and seating.
Yes — please do! Bellevue Botanical Garden is open to the public all afternoon and is a beautiful place to wander. Arrive whenever you like, take in the pathways and plantings, and make an evening of it. The Aaron Education Center doors open at 5:30 PM for Golden Hour Unboxed check-in; the program begins at 6:00 PM.
Yes — all ages are welcome, and families are encouraged to come together. The evening is designed to work across generations. The Garden is a living collection, so please keep everyone on the paths and keep an eye on little ones near the plantings. There is no dedicated childcare or kids programming, but there is plenty of open space and room to move. Strollers do fine on the main pathways.
Golden Hour Unboxed is designed as an unhurried, flowing evening at Bellevue Botanical Garden's education facility — most guests stand, stroll, and mingle their way through the program. Tables are set up for vendors, food, and the Micro Speed Pitching Showcase. Accessible seating is set up inside the Aaron Education Center, and there are benches and seating areas throughout the Garden grounds. If you'd like to request accessibility accommodations in advance, email katoya@toyboxconsulting.net.
Because we are in peak summer season at the Bellevue Botanical Garden, we have reserved overflow parking for our guests at Wilburton Instructional Service Center (WISC) · 12241 Main St, Bellevue WA 98005 — a short walk east of the Garden along Main St. Look for Golden Hour Unboxed signage as you arrive. Build a few extra minutes into your arrival window to make the walk over comfortably. Carpooling and rideshare are still encouraged. We are expecting a big turnout, so if you can arrive before 5:30 you will have an easier time parking — and so will everyone behind you.
Yes. Most of the main Garden pathways are packed gravel built to meet ADA standards, so they work for wheelchairs and walkers. There are several disabled parking spots in the Garden’s lot, and accessible restrooms near the Trillium Store. The Garden does not have wheelchairs available to loan, so please bring your own equipment. Inside the Aaron Education Center we will have seating for anyone who needs it, and our team can help you find a spot. If you have a specific accessibility need, email katoya@toyboxconsulting.net ahead of the event and we will make arrangements. For the facility itself, the Garden’s own accessibility page is the best source: bellevuebotanical.org/accessibility.
Service animals are welcome. Pets are not permitted at Bellevue Botanical Garden, so please leave the dogs at home for this one. That is the Garden’s rule and it applies to every visitor.
Bellevue Botanical Garden runs its own site with everything about the facility — hours, maps, parking, accessibility, the Trillium Store, and what is in bloom: bellevuebotanical.org. We are guests there on August 23. The Garden is open to the public that same day, so other visitors will be enjoying it alongside us.
Pitch slots for August 23 are closed and the lineup is set. Three founders will each take two minutes, with live feedback from our judges. Come watch — it is one of the best twenty-five minutes of the evening.
Tabling is closed for August 23 and all twenty-one tables are booked — Black-owned businesses and makers selling inside, community organizations out in the garden. We would still love to hear from you for what comes next: email katoya@toyboxconsulting.net.
We welcome partnership conversations at any level. Whether you're interested in being a presenting partner, programming sponsor, community supporter, in-kind contributor, or media partner — we'd love to design something together. Reach out to katoya@toyboxconsulting.net for our sponsor & partner outreach kit.
The event happens. Sunday, August 23 is firm, and the Aaron Education Center is indoors — so smoke, rain, or heat will not cancel Golden Hour Unboxed.

What would change is the shape of the evening. Much of the experience is built around being outdoors: the Garden, the patio, the way the vendor village breathes across the space. If air quality, heat, or rain makes the outdoors unwise, we will move the program and the layout inside and adjust the run of show accordingly.

If conditions look uncertain in the days before the event, check this website — it is where we post the most current plan, and we will send the same information by email and social media. Please check before you leave the house on the 23rd.
We are expecting a big turnout, and that is a good problem. Golden Hour Unboxed is built à la carte — there is no single moment you have to be seated for. Four things are happening: the Garden itself, the vendor village, the Micro Speed Pitching Showcase, and the Pack the Box drive. Take them in whatever order suits you.

The most useful thing you can do is spread out your arrival. Doors open at 5:30 and the program begins at 6:00, so the heaviest crowding will be right at six. If you come earlier and walk the Garden first, you will have a better evening — and so will everyone behind you. Wander, come back, sit down, go out again. Nothing is missed by moving at your own pace.
Bellevue Botanical Garden is a living collection and a public garden, open to other visitors that same day. Please stay on the paths, leave the plantings alone, keep an eye on little ones near the beds, and take your cups and plates with you. Treat it the way you would someone's home, because that is closer to the truth than a venue rental. We would very much like to be invited back.
Pack the Box is our back-to-school drive, and everything collected goes to the schools with the highest need, PreK through high school. Bring anything new and unwrapped to the registration table when you arrive.

Bellevue and most neighboring districts now provide required classroom supplies, so the most useful gifts are the things they don't cover — backpacks, headphones, hygiene items, adaptive and sensory supplies, and the classroom items teachers buy with their own money. Gift cards are the easiest of all. See the full list of supply ideas.
Garden casual — think effortless evening wear. Layers are recommended as the temperature can shift from the warm afternoon into a cooler twilight. Shoes you can stand and stroll in, since most of the evening is spent on your feet. If the sun is out, a parasol, sun hat or sunglasses makes the walk through the garden much more comfortable, and the light at that hour is worth being outside for. Check the forecast the day before — we post updates at goldenhourunboxed.com/updates. The botanical setting invites a celebratory, culturally expressive aesthetic — wear what makes you feel beautiful and yourself.
